author: desk
note: Desk-written plain-English summary, not a tiered fact. Written to help a reader understand the business quickly; verify any figure against the fact store before using it in a report.
one_liner: Sells AI models to large enterprises, especially where data cannot leave the building.
what_it_does: Cohere builds language models aimed squarely at business use, with an emphasis on deployment inside a customer's own infrastructure. It concentrates on banking, healthcare, telecoms and government, where privacy rules make public interfaces difficult.
how_it_makes_money: Enterprise licences and private deployments, plus a developer interface. Fewer, larger contracts than a consumer-facing peer.
why_it_matters: It is the test of whether a mid-sized lab can survive by serving regulated industries rather than competing at the frontier.
competitive_position: Competes with the frontier labs' enterprise offerings and with open-weight models a customer can host free. Its advantage is deployment flexibility, not raw model quality.
key_risks: It is outspent on training by an order of magnitude.
Open-weight models are a free substitute for the privacy use case.
Enterprise sales cycles are long and expensive.
Revenue is well behind the frontier labs on a similar valuation basis.

glossary.definition: Running the model inside the customer's own environment so their data never leaves it.
Letting a model look things up in a company's own documents before answering, rather than relying on memory.
